content: Keep the desktop UI's established look, which the user approved on 2026-10-08. It has a navy brand header (--brand #1f3a5f), a light canvas (#f2f4f7) with white panels, an 8px radius, and Segoe UI text with Cascadia Mono for code. The results list sits on the left (20–26rem) and the part detail on the right. The window itself never scrolls; only panels and columns do. Inside the part detail, a header sits on top. Below it, the symbol and footprint are stacked on the left and share the height, and every catalog field is always visible on the right, with no collapsible. Long URL values stay on one line with an ellipsis. Symbols render on KiCad's light schematic paper and footprints on KiCad's dark board (#001023). Each error state has one alert, and supporting notes stay quiet. Reuse the tokens in apps/desktop-ui/styles.css rather than adding colours, and extend this layout rather than redesigning it.

title: Sign in to the team catalog with an in-memory session, loopback only for now
rationale: The desktop saves only the team server address and email (config/team.json); the password is sent once to auth-with-password and the session token stays in memory, so nothing secret is stored and a restart asks for the password again. Only http://127.0.0.1, localhost or [::1] are accepted because collaboration's realtime client speaks plain HTTP and a password must not cross a network unencrypted; a shared server needs HTTPS realtime first. Edit access is the users field can_edit_catalog, which members cannot set on themselves.

description: A component class with display:flex (.team-tabs) overrode the HTML hidden attribute, so tabs meant to hide behind the conflict view stayed visible; the journey's el.hidden check still passed.
resolution: styles.css ends with [hidden] { display: none !important; }. Journey 06 checks layout (getClientRects().length === 0), not the hidden property.

description: In Leptos 0.8.3, calling .track() on a Memo inside an Effect did not re-run the Effect when the memo's source changed (the search did not refresh after a team Change), while .get() on an equivalent memo elsewhere worked.
resolution: Read the memo's value in the Effect (let _ = memo.get();) instead of only tracking it; .track() is fine on RwSignals (apps/desktop-ui/src/main.rs search effect).

title: The team column shows shared part details and the current revision apart; one Edit part form
rationale:
Seed kicad-parts-7556, chosen for the simplest product without asking the user (who asked for best judgement); revised after review. Wording below is exactly what apps/desktop-ui/src/team.rs and main.rs show.

Revision wording: the part's own revision reads 'revision N of this part' (header Source fact 'Team catalog, revision N of this part'; Details heading 'Symbol and footprint (revision N of this part)'). A CAD item's own revision reads 'symbol revision N' or 'footprint revision N' (binding rows such as 'g-pas:R_US, symbol revision 1', history change rows, preview labels 'team catalog, symbol revision N', fallback notes 'Symbol revision N of <ref> could not be fetched ...'), so the two never read alike. History entries keep 'Revision N · ...', since there it can only be the part's.

Details tab: 'Part details (N)' with the 'Edit part' button (or 'You can view this part but not edit it.'), the hint 'Every revision of the part shares these details.', the fields table, 'Manufacturer parts', then 'Symbol and footprint (revision N of this part)' (or 'This part uses no symbol or footprint.'). No separate list of other revisions: the history already lists every revision.

One 'Edit part' form, not two: heading 'Edit part', hint 'Change details only to correct them. A part with a different value, package or pinout needs a new IPN.', fieldsets 'Part details', 'Manufacturer parts (the first is the main one)', and 'Symbol and footprint' with the hint 'Changing these adds a new revision of this part. Designs that use revision N keep it.' When someone else saves meanwhile: 'Someone else saved a change to this part while you were editing. When you save, you can compare your changes with theirs.' Save notices: 'Saved. The part details changed; no revision was added.' or 'Saved as revision N.'

History: one entry per Change, titled 'Part details · Edited by X' or 'Revision N · Imported by an administrator', with ' (current)' on the entry that added the current revision. The selected entry shows 'What changed in revision N' or 'What changed in the part details' with Field/Before/After rows (details rows first); revision 1 says 'The first revision of this part.'

Conflict screen: one heading 'Someone else changed this part first', the line 'X saved a change on <time> ("reason") after you started editing. Your changes are not saved yet.', one table with columns Field / You started from / Theirs / Yours ('not changed' where you changed nothing), the hint 'Saving on top keeps their changes and adds yours. Where you both changed a field, yours is kept.', and buttons 'Save my changes on top of theirs', 'Edit again', 'Discard my changes'. Deliberate simplification: one heading and one table cover both sections, while the behaviour stays per section (only rows of what moved or what you changed appear, and saving on top resends only the sections you changed).

Archive (kicad-parts-5bea): a selected revision entry in History offers 'Archive revision N…' or, when archived, 'Unarchive revision N…' (editors only). It opens a small form 'Archive revision N' with 'KiCad and this app stop offering revision N, so nobody new picks it. Designs that already use it keep it. Nothing is deleted. The current revision becomes (or stays) revision X.' (unarchive: 'KiCad and this app offer revision N again. The current revision becomes revision X.'), 'Why are you archiving it?' and a reason. The only revision not archived shows 'Revision N is the only revision that is not archived, so it cannot be archived. Add a corrected revision first.' instead of a button, so the refusal comes before submitting. Notices: 'Revision N is archived. The current revision is now revision X.' / 'Revision N is no longer archived. The current revision is now revision X.' History entries read 'Revision N · Archived by X' (selected: 'Revision N archived', 'Revision N was archived. The current revision became revision X.'), and revision entries carry ' (archived)' as they carry ' (current)'. The Details tab ends with 'Other revisions: revision 1 (older), revision 3 (archived).' when there are others. Styles reuse the existing tokens; the new rules are '.archive-form' (the light panel the removed restore form used: #f5f7fa, --line border, --radius), '.archive-open', '.team-toolbar + .hint { margin: 0 0 0.5rem; }' (the line under a section heading) and '.binding { white-space: nowrap; }' (a binding such as 'footprint revision 1' stays on one line, so a long reference breaks after its comma).
